mappings.note: Bioluminescence named as light produced by chemical reactions inside an organism: a phenomenon explained rather than a change to be sorted, so LO-54 not LO-51.

Paper sits in oxygen without burning because nothing has raised it to its ignition temperature: a non-event traced to the missing cause. Not LO-54, since the item turns on one condition rather than the whole process.
Defines ignition temperature, a term that belongs to the explanation of how combustion starts.
Traces the mechanism from focused sunlight to concentrated heat to ignition: the process explained end to end.
Fuel, oxygen and heat as the fire triangle: the conditions that make up the explanation of combustion.
Melting wax placed as a physical change: the composition is unchanged.
Burning wax vapour placed as a chemical change because new substances form. Companion to the melting item, and the pair is the point of the candle example.
Summarises the candle as physical melting plus chemical burning, i.e. the both-kinds category.
Michael Faraday and his Chemical History of a Candle lectures: a story of a scientist to be appreciated. Not LO-54, because nothing about burning is explained in the answer.
Defines a reversible change as one where the original can be got back, a criterion for sorting changes.
Burning wood is irreversible because ash and gases cannot be reassembled: the same sorting criterion applied.
Names the desirable category for useful changes such as cooking and ripening: another axis on which the chapter sorts changes.
Names the undesirable category for rusting and spoilage, the counterpart of the previous item.
Shows that the same decomposition counts as undesirable spoilage or desirable composting depending on context, which is about how the category is assigned, not about composting itself, so not LO-62.
Weathering named as the set of processes that break rock down over time. A process named, so LO-54; the items that ask whether a particular weathering is physical or chemical are on LO-51.
Temperature swings, root growth and freezing water are sorted as physical weathering because composition is unchanged.
The red layer on basalt is sorted as chemical weathering because iron minerals have reacted: same sorting task, opposite verdict.
Erosion named as the transport of weathered material by wind and water: a named process, like weathering.
Erosion judged physical because material is only moved, not chemically altered. Classification, unlike the item that merely names the process.
Assertion and reason both rest on the no-new-substance criterion for physical change, illustrated by melting ice.
Picks grinding wheat as the irreversible one among four changes, sorting by reversibility.
Leaves decomposing into compost placed as chemical because microorganisms produce new substances.
Magnesium oxide assigned to the basic class. A material placed by a property, which LO-51 covers; no equation is asked for, so not LO-55.
Curdling judged chemical from the changed taste and smell that signal new substances.
The compost step of the Prithvi story placed as a chemical change.
Germination and growth placed as chemical because photosynthesis and metabolism build new tissue.
Decides which of four set-ups will turn lime water milky, which is predicting and reading experimental results. Not LO-51, because no change is labelled.
Places the burning candle in the overlap region of the Venn diagram, a classification item.
Lemon-juice ink appears because the acid chars before the paper does when heated: the effect traced to its cause. Not LO-51, since the item asks for the principle rather than the label.
Identifies the gas from the yeast project by the inflating balloon and the milky lime water: a conclusion drawn from two pieces of evidence.
Fermentation placed as a chemical change because ethanol and carbon dioxide are new substances.
Soil formation placed in the both-physical-and-chemical category.
Assertion and reason both concern reaching ignition temperature, with the lens as the means: an explanation of how combustion is started.
Melting ice against burning wood on both axes, physical or chemical and reversible or not: a two-way classification.
Picks change of state as the one indicator that does not signal a chemical change, which tests the boundary between the two categories.
Names the physical-change category from its definition.
No new substance in a physical change: the defining criterion in one word.
Names the chemical-change category from its definition.
Chemical reaction named as the process behind a chemical change. A process named rather than a change sorted, so LO-54.
Lime water going milky is the observed result of the carbon dioxide test.
Calcium carbonate named as the product of the lime water reaction: the reaction-product outcome, not the observation.
Carbon dioxide named as the product of vinegar with baking soda.
Rusting placed as a chemical change.
Iron oxide named as the substance rusting produces, which is the corrosion reaction LO-55 lists. The companion item that only asks for the category is on LO-51.
Combustion named as reaction with oxygen giving heat and light: a process named, matching the other combustion items.
